info.name: EventMitra API
info.description: Main-module permission flow: login as your super admin, create role, create admin with that role, create main module, assign per-admin flags, and save the matrix. Login and auth/me return effective module permissions. No submodules. Codes are generated. Credentials remain empty in the local environment. Permission POST accepts an object or array and upserts existing rows. Login accepts email or username. New admins require admin_username. Names and identities are checked for duplicates. Migration 014: admin user/owner CRUD and bank account add/list/get/update are in a separate folder. Ordinary admins require user_management/owner_management module actions; super admins have access.

request.description: identifier accepts email or username. You may instead send email or username, but provide exactly one login field. Usernames contain no spaces. Set admin_login in the environment; legacy admin_email is used as a fallback.

exec: const resolve = value => typeof value === 'string' ? pm.variables.replaceIn(value) : Array.isArray(value) ? value.map(resolve) : value && typeof value === 'object' ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).map(([key, child]) => [key, resolve(child)])) : value;

pm.test('Login returns module flags', function () { const data=pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(data.permissions).to.be.an('array'); if(data.permissions.length) pm.expect(data.permissions[0]).to.have.keys('module_id','module_code','module_key','module_name','all','create','read','edit','delete','view'); });
